info.description: Autonomous, governed data & analytics agent operating system (Phase 1 MVP).
info.title: Context2AI AnalystOS

post.description:
Rebuild the registry from every source and swap it in. A load that fails leaves the current
registry in place (the error lists every problem). Runs in flight keep the versions they bound.
Reloads this process; other processes (worker, scheduler) reload on their own call.

get.description: Effective routing after admin overrides: purpose -> mode, profile, candidate models, availability.
Tokens spent vs avoided (cache hits, deterministic skips, refused oversize prompts).
Download to the requesting user (audited). Sending outside the platform would need an approval.

post.description: Publishing is proposal-based: returns the pending, hash-bound proposal that includes this artifact.

Ask in a thread. With `Accept: text/event-stream` the plain-language stages stream as `stage`
events, then `turn` (the persisted answer or refusal) and `end`; otherwise the turn is returned.

Promote an answer: verified query, metric, monitor, "Investigate why" (starts a run), or a
dashboard chart (202 with an approval request first; again with the approved `approval_id`).

patch.description: A person's curation wins over every crawler/model description from now on.

get.description:
Validate the transaction, exchange the code with the verifier, validate the ID token and
provision the user. The browser returns to the web app with the AnalystOS token in the URL
fragment (never sent to a server); `Accept: application/json` gets the login response instead.

Start the authorization-code flow: state, nonce and a PKCE verifier go into a short-lived signed
HttpOnly cookie; the browser is sent to the IdP with the S256 challenge only.
What the login screen offers: password sign-in and/or single sign-on.

The generated dbt project file by file against the previous job for the same target (or `against`,
another job of the same workspace). Read-only: what the approver reviews, not what they approve —
the approval binds the whole project hash.
Every registered capability, filtered by kind; with `workspace_id`, its enablement there.

post.description:
The user says what kind the feedback really was. Recorded to calibrate feedback_classification;
submit the feedback again with an explicit kind to act on it.

get.description: Dependency health. Reports what is reachable; never claims readiness it cannot observe.

patch.description: Retire a question so scheduled re-analysis stops replaying it (or reactivate it).

get.description: Evidence behind a finding (DoD #20): experiments, queries (with SQL and result preview), lineage.

post.description: Accept or dismiss a finding (a rejection goes through run feedback, which also replans).

get.description: Per model call of a run: the purpose and the receipts of the context it carried.

Every database/file/API kind the platform can connect, with the fields a form needs,
whether its driver is installed and enabled by the administrator, and whether it is certified
(a dated live-run evidence file exists; connectors/certification.py).
Agent console (§52.7): messages, tool calls, model calls, queries, cost.

Persisted event stream as Server-Sent Events. Reconnect with ?after_id=<last id> (or Last-Event-ID).
Database reads run in worker threads; new events arrive by Redis nudge (polling only as a fallback).

post.description:
Run a capability with arguments validated against its `input_schema`. Read-only capabilities run
now; any other side effect returns 202 with an approval request, and runs only when called again
with that approval once it is approved (verified against the exact payload just before running).

get.description: Searchable catalog built by the crawler (names, business names, descriptions, role/domain).

post.description: Dashboards are produced by an analysis run (design -> approval -> publish). This starts one.

What the context compiler would send for `purpose` about `question` from this workspace's
knowledge (the catalog section is left out: it depends on a run's scope). No model is called.

get.description: The review queue: drafts with per-field value, confidence and provenance.

post.description: Approve, edit-then-approve or reject drafts in one batch: one workspace-pack revision.
Manual SQL console: same gateway, same scope and audit as agents (no bypass).

Deterministic explanation (no model, no execution), the gateway validator's verdict for this
caller and, when accepted, the source's plan through the gateway (EXPLAIN only).

get.description: `osi/*.json` files for a dbt 1.12 project (approved metrics only) and what dbt would object to.
Approved metrics as Superset dataset-metric payloads (what the Superset publisher writes).

post.description: Body: the content of dbt's `target/osi_document.json`. Metrics arrive as proposals.
Body: {"document": "<an Ossie 0.1.1 document, YAML or JSON>"}. Metrics arrive as proposals.

Check a proposal without recording it (the KPI editor's live validation): field problems and the
conflicts it would create. Proposing still re-checks everything.

get.description: The workspace model as an Apache Ossie 0.1.1 document (YAML download, or JSON).

post.description: Promote a successful Ask answer (`query_id` + `question`) or a verified finding (`insight_id`).
